speakers: The voice of the Lord to Nephi
meta.audience: Nephi alone, and then the scattered multitudes
meta.location: The road to Nephi's house, and the land at large
principles: A blessing given for what was already done
An errand taken up before reaching home

world_behind.title: The crowd leaves him standing there
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has the people dividing and going their ways after the events of Helaman 9, with Nephi alone in the middle.

world_behind.title: The revelation comes while walking
world_behind.text: Verses 2 and 3 have him heading home, pondering, and much cast down, when a voice comes. 1 Nephi 11:1 has Nephi caught away while sitting and pondering, and Alma 8:14 and 15 have an angel meet Alma on the road as he journeys weighed down with sorrow. The record puts three of its revelations in the same posture: alone, moving, and discouraged.

world_behind.title: The blessing names a quality
world_behind.text: Verses 4 and 5 use "unwearyingness" twice, and the word occurs nowhere else in scripture. Helaman 15:6 has Samuel praise the converted Lamanites for "unwearied diligence," which is the nearest the record comes to it anywhere else.

world_behind.title: The promise has a stated limit
world_behind.text: Verse 5 puts every thing at his word, and gives the reason: he will not ask contrary to God's will. Verse 7 then grants the sealing power in the words of Matthew 16:19, which is the only place in the volume that formula appears.

world_behind.title: The sealing power is granted in the words of Matthew 16:19
world_behind.text: Verse 7 uses seal and loose where the gospel uses bind and loose, with the same on-earth and in-heaven structure.

world_behind.title: He turns around before arriving
world_behind.text: Verse 12 has him stopping short of his own house and going back to the scattered people. Verse 2 had him walking home from the crowd that dispersed in verse 1, so the chapter runs a complete round trip in eleven verses and puts the commission at the far end of it.

world_behind.title: He is carried from crowd to crowd
world_behind.text: Verses 16 and 17 have the Spirit removing him from an arrest and moving him among all the people until every one had heard. Helaman 5:43 to 49 had delivered him and his brother from a Lamanite prison by fire and a cloud of darkness; 3 Nephi 28:19 to 22 reports the same kind of deliverance for the three disciples three centuries later.

words.text: Treated at 1 Nephi 11:1, where the first Nephi is caught away while sitting and pondering. The record uses the word eleven times, twice in this chapter, and both Nephis receive a revelation in that posture.
Working without tiring or slackening. The word occurs twice in all of scripture, at verses 4 and 5 of this chapter, and nowhere else. It is the quality the blessing is given for.
Treated at 2 Nephi 16:2, of the seraphim wings. The record uses the word ten times and the King James Bible seventeen, including the temple veil at Mark 15:38, which is the object named here.
All-powerful. The record uses the title thirteen times and the King James Bible fifty-seven. Verse 11 attaches it to the message Nephi is sent back to deliver.
A work beyond natural power. The record uses the singular eight times. Verse 13 applies it to the naming of Seantum and reports that it changed nothing.
Carried from one place to another. It appears once in the record, and once in the King James Bible, at John 5:13. It describes how Nephi left a crowd that was reaching for him.

phrases.term: They divided hither and thither and went their ways, leaving Nephi alone
phrases.text: The aftermath of Helaman 9. A murder solved by prophecy ends with the crowd dispersing and the prophet standing by himself.

phrases.term: Pondering upon the things which the Lord had shown unto him
phrases.text: What he does with a day like that one. The walk home is where the next revelation finds him.

phrases.term: Being much cast down because of the wickedness of the people
phrases.text: Mormon gives the state he was in when the voice came. The blessing arrives on a discouraged man.

phrases.term: Thou hast with unwearyingness declared the word
phrases.text: The reason for the blessing, given first. Verse 4 lists three more: he did not fear them, did not seek his own life, and sought God's will.

phrases.term: Thou shalt not ask that which is contrary to my will
phrases.text: The limit that makes the promise safe to give. The power is unlimited in form and bounded by the character of the man holding it.

phrases.term: Behold, thou art Nephi, and I am God
phrases.text: Two identities stated in one line. Some of the people had just called him a god in Helaman 9:41, and this sentence sorts that out.

phrases.term: Whatsoever ye shall seal on earth shall be sealed in heaven
phrases.text: The grant itself. Matthew 16:19 gives Peter the same structure with bind in place of seal.

phrases.term: If ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou cast down and become smooth, it shall be done
phrases.text: The illustration of scale. The first Nephi had made the same kind of statement about water and earth in 1 Nephi 17:50.

phrases.term: He did stop and did not go unto his own house
phrases.text: The hinge of the chapter. He was almost home, and the errand sent him back the way he came.

phrases.term: He was taken by the Spirit and conveyed away out of the midst of them
phrases.text: Rescue by removal. The men reaching to imprison him find nobody there.

phrases.term: They were divided against themselves and began to slay one another with the sword
phrases.text: The chapter's last event. The division of verse 1 becomes a civil killing by verse 18.

verses.label: v. 2–3
verses.title: A revelation that arrives on a walk home
verses.text: The record fixes the setting before it reports the voice, and the setting is ordinary: "Nephi went his way towards his own house, pondering upon the things which the Lord had shown unto him." Verse 3 adds his state of mind and it is not elevated: "being much cast down because of the wickedness of the people of the Nephites, their secret works of darkness, and their murderings, and their plunderings." Only then does the voice come. Nothing about the moment is arranged, and the record supplies the mood as part of the circumstances.

verses.label: v. 4–5
verses.title: One invented word, used twice and nowhere else
verses.text: The blessing turns on a noun that appears in these two verses and in no other verse of scripture: "I have beheld how thou hast with unwearyingness declared the word," and "because thou hast done this with such unwearyingness, behold, I will bless thee forever." The related adjective unwearied stands once more, at Hel. 15:6, of the Lamanite missionaries. The record reaches for a word it has to build in order to name the quality it is rewarding.

verses.label: v. 6–7
verses.title: A grant given in the words of another Gospel
verses.text: The authority is conferred in a formula that stands at Matt. 16:19: "whatsoever ye shall seal on earth shall be sealed in heaven; and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven." The King James verse reads bind where this reads seal, and the second half matches word for word. The record offers no source. Verse 6 also states the reason for the grant, and it is a prediction about the man rather than a reward: "thou shalt not ask that which is contrary to my will."

verses.label: v. 11–12
verses.title: Obedience reported by an interrupted journey
verses.text: The record measures the response by what did not happen: "when the Lord had spoken these words unto Nephi, he did stop and did not go unto his own house, but did return unto the multitudes." Verse 2 had him walking home. The verse that reports his obedience does it by cancelling that errand, and the detail of the unreached house is the only evidence the chapter gives for the speed of his compliance.

verses.label: v. 13
verses.title: A miracle that changed nothing, and the record says so
verses.text: One verse concedes the failure of the previous chapter's proof: "notwithstanding that great miracle which Nephi had done in telling them concerning the death of the chief judge, they did harden their hearts and did not hearken unto the words of the Lord." Helaman 9 ended with four different groups drawing four conclusions from a verified prediction. This verse reports the net effect on the population, and it is nil.

verses.label: v. 16–17
verses.title: An escape described as transport
verses.text: The record gives the mechanism twice: "the power of God was with him, and they could not take him to cast him into prison, for he was taken by the Spirit and conveyed away out of the midst of them." Verse 17 makes it a method rather than a single rescue: "thus he did go forth in the Spirit, from multitude to multitude, declaring the word of God, even until he had declared it unto them all." What began as a deliverance from arrest becomes the way the preaching tour is conducted.

chapter.title: The blessing is for the past, not the future
chapter.text: Verse 4 gives four reasons, all of them things already done. The power in verse 7 arrives as a consequence of a track record.

chapter.title: Unwearyingness is the named quality
chapter.text: Not eloquence, courage, or results. The word exists nowhere else in scripture and describes continuing to do the thing.

chapter.title: The limit is the man's own will
chapter.text: Verse 5 secures an unlimited promise by observing that he will not ask wrongly. Character does the work a restriction would otherwise do.

chapter.title: Verse 6 answers Helaman 9:41
chapter.text: People had concluded he was a god. The voice tells him plainly which of them is which.

chapter.title: He never gets home
chapter.text: Verse 2 has him walking there and verse 12 has him turning around. Alma 8:16 has an angel sending a prophet back the same way.

chapter.title: The miracle changed nothing
chapter.text: Verse 13 notes the great miracle and the hardened hearts in one sentence. The chapter treats evidence as insufficient by itself.

chapter.title: The Spirit moves him rather than protecting him in place
chapter.text: Verses 16 and 17 have removal and transport used as one thing, so the rescue becomes the next assignment.

chapter.title: The chapter opens and closes on division
chapter.text: Verse 1 has them dividing and walking away, verse 18 has them dividing and killing. Ten verses of revelation sit between the two.

applications.title: Keep going when nobody stays
applications.text: The crowd dispersed and left him standing there, and the next thing that happened was the blessing. Being left alone is not a verdict on the work.

applications.title: Take the long walk
applications.text: He went home pondering rather than rehearsing. Unhurried thinking after a hard day is where verse 3 happens.

applications.title: Let unwearyingness be the goal
applications.text: He was commended for not slackening. Steady continuation is a quality you can actually choose, unlike outcomes.

applications.title: Read the condition inside the promise
applications.text: The grant that all things shall be done according to his word arrives with a clause attached: he will not ask what is contrary to God's will. Wide authority in this record comes fastened to a character that will not misuse it.

applications.title: Turn around before you get home
applications.text: He stopped short and went back. When the assignment lands, acting on it while it is fresh costs less than resuming it tomorrow.

applications.title: Do not expect the proof to do the work
applications.text: They had just watched Nephi name the death of the chief judge, and they hardened their hearts anyway. Evidence moves a mind that is open, and it cannot supply the opening.

applications.title: Count who has heard, not how often you spoke
applications.text: Nephi went in the Spirit from multitude to multitude until he had declared the word to all of them. When a message matters, measure the coverage rather than your own effort.

applications.title: A refused correction moves inward
applications.text: They would not hearken, and the contentions that followed had them slaying one another. An argument a group will not settle with the outside does not go away; it relocates.

questions.text: What am I still doing after the people who joined me left?
What am I cast down about right now?
Where in my life would unwearyingness be the honest word?
If I could have whatever I asked, what would I ask for?
What errand am I postponing until after I get home?
What evidence have I received and not acted on?
What division around me is getting sharper while I wait?

entries.head: Hel. 9:36

anchor.quote: thou hast not feared them, and hast not sought thine own life

entries.reason: the claim Nephi staked his life on the day before

targets.quote: then shall ye know that I am an honest man, and that I am sent unto you from God.
targets.verse_text: And then shall he say unto you, that I, Nephi, know nothing concerning the matter save it were given unto me by the power of God. And then shall ye know that I am an honest man, and that I am sent unto you from God.
targets.markdown: And then shall he say unto you, that I, Nephi, know nothing concerning the matter save it were given unto me by the power of God. And **then shall ye know that I am an honest man, and that I am sent unto you from God**.

targets.markdown: O Lord, do not suffer that this people shall be destroyed by the sword; but O Lord, **rather let there be a famine in the land, to stir them up in remembrance of the Lord their God**, and perhaps they will repent and turn unto thee.

targets.markdown: And there were others who said: Behold, **he is a god, for except he was a god he could not know of all things**. For behold, he has told us the thoughts of our hearts, and also has told us things; and even he has brought unto our knowledge the true murderer of our chief judge.

targets.markdown: For it came to pass after I had desired to know the things that my father had seen, and believing that the Lord was able to make them known unto me, **as I sat pondering in mine heart I was caught away in the Spirit of the Lord**, yea, into an exceedingly high mountain, which I never had before seen, and upon which I never had before set my foot.
